Run several recipes over one document and compare them

Source: R/doc-bench-compare.R
gr_compare.Rd

Each recipe is an independent pipeline, so a recipe's answer is identical whether it is run alone or alongside others. Extraction is shared through the ingest cache, and segmentation is shared between recipes whose segment specs are identical, so comparing five readers over one chunking costs one chunking, not five.

Usage

gr_compare(
  source,
  question,
  recipes = c("fast", "needle", "thorough"),
  client = NULL,
  allow_duplicates = FALSE,
  on_error = c("continue", "stop"),
  correct = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

source

File path, web address, or raw text; see gr_ingest().

question

The question.

recipes

A character vector of recipe names, or a list of gr_recipes.

client

A gr_client.

allow_duplicates

Run duplicates anyway (useful at temperature > 0 to measure variance).

on_error

"continue" keeps going and records the failure; "stop" aborts the whole comparison.

correct

How to tell whether an answer is right, for the correct and usd_per_correct columns. NULL (the default) adds neither. A character vector marks an answer right when its text contains any of the strings, ignoring case and runs of white space; an answer that found nothing, or a recipe that failed, is wrong, and one that found nothing because a limit stopped it is NA: the spending, token or call limit, the model allow-list or the output ceiling. A function is called with each recipe's gr_answer and returns TRUE, FALSE or NA (not known); when it fails or returns anything else, a warning of class gr_bad_correct names the recipe and its correct is NA. An invalid correct argument is an error of the same class.

...

Overrides applied to every recipe.

Value

A list with answers (named list of gr_answer), summary, trace (shared across all recipes, so it records every recipe's calls) and document (source and ingestion stats). summary is a data frame with one row per recipe and these columns:

recipe, segmenter, chunks, reader, signature, settings

Which pipeline the row is, and what was changed from the recipe's defaults.

partial, chunks_used, answer_chars, not_found, error

What the answer is, and what went wrong, if anything.

calls, tokens_in, tokens_out

The model and embeddings requests the recipe made, its segmentation's included, and the tokens of those that were billed: a request answered from a cache or a recording is counted in calls and costs nothing.

usd

What those requests cost, at the prices registered with gr_register_model(). NA when a model the recipe used has no registered price.

usd_estimated

The share of usd spent on requests whose token counts were estimated locally because the provider reported none, from 0 to 1. NA when no request records how its counts were obtained, or when usd is 0 or unknown.

correct, usd_per_correct

Only with correct: whether the answer was right, and usd divided by the number of right answers, which is usd for a right answer, Inf for a wrong one that cost something and NA for a wrong one that cost nothing or one whose correctness is not known.

premise

Only when a recipe checks the question's premise: what the model said the document states instead, or NA; see premise in gr_read_spec().

Details

Recipes that resolve to identical ingestion, identical segmentation and an identical read spec are collapsed with a warning rather than billed twice. A shared reader signature alone is not enough: two retrieve recipes with different top_k share a signature and are genuinely different runs.

Each row of summary says what its recipe cost, priced from the requests on the trace by the model each one used (see gr_trace_cost()). A recipe is charged what it would cost run alone: a segmentation it shares with an earlier recipe is charged to both, as max_calls counts it for both, so sum(summary$usd) can be more than the comparison spent, which is sum(gr_trace_cost(trace)$usd). Give correct and each row also says whether the answer was right and what a right answer cost.

A comparison is one run for the spending and token limits: max_cost_usd and max_tokens_total in gr_options() are checked against what every recipe and every segmentation has spent and used so far, so a recipe that reaches either limit stops partial and the ones after it are refused and recorded as failed. max_calls is counted for each recipe on its own, its segmentation included, so a recipe's answer does not depend on its position in the list. A segmentation that a limit cut short is not shared with a later recipe.

See also

answer_document(), gr_recipes(), gr_recipe(), gr_answer

Examples

cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")

# Three pipelines over one document. Extraction is shared, so this costs one
# extraction, not three; only the segmentation and the reader vary.
cmp <- gr_compare(gr_example(), "What was revenue?",
                  c("fast", "precise", "needle"), client = cl)
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'paragraph' (cap 4000 tokens, overlap 0).
#> Reading with 'stuff' (all|1|none) over 1 chunk(s).
#> Segmenting with 'sentence' (cap 600 tokens, overlap 60).
#> Reading with 'skim' (all|N+1|none) over 2 chunk(s).
#> Segmenting with 'semantic' (cap 500 tokens, overlap 50).
#> Reading with 'retrieve' (topk|1|none) over 2 chunk(s).
cmp$summary[, c("recipe", "segmenter", "chunks", "reader", "signature", "chunks_used")]
#>    recipe segmenter chunks   reader    signature chunks_used
#> 1    fast paragraph      1    stuff   all|1|none           1
#> 2 precise  sentence      2     skim all|N+1|none           2
#> 3  needle  semantic      2 retrieve  topk|1|none           2

# One trace covers all three, so this is the cost of the whole comparison.
gr_trace_summary(cmp$trace)
#>                          run_id calls cached steps tokens_in tokens_out errors
#> 1 run_20261106065720.632_c36688     5      0    16      2122         65      0
#>   elapsed_s embed_calls embed_tokens tokens_reasoning tokens_cached_in
#> 1      0.32           0            0                0                0
#>   usage_estimated
#> 1               1

# What each recipe cost, and what a right answer cost. The mock is free, so
# register a price for it under another name to see the columns filled.
gr_register_model("priced-mock", context_window = 128000, max_output = 4096,
                  input_usd = 2, output_usd = 8)
cmp <- gr_compare(gr_example(), "What was revenue?", c("fast", "precise"),
                  client = cl, model = "priced-mock", correct = "45.2 million")
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'paragraph' (cap 4000 tokens, overlap 0).
#> Reading with 'stuff' (all|1|none) over 1 chunk(s).
#> Segmenting with 'sentence' (cap 600 tokens, overlap 60).
#> Reading with 'skim' (all|N+1|none) over 2 chunk(s).
cmp$summary[, c("recipe", "calls", "usd", "correct", "usd_per_correct")]
#>    recipe calls      usd correct usd_per_correct
#> 1    fast     1 0.001318    TRUE        0.001318
#> 2 precise     3 0.001998    TRUE        0.001998
